question.text: Will Ituri province report at least 10 more new confirmed Ebola cases than Nord-Kivu province for 26 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the daily Ebola situation report (SitRep) published by the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) with reporting date 26 November 2026 (expected to be SitRep N°196, published on 27 November 2026), available at https://insp.cd/ and archived at https://ebola-tracker.org/en/reports. Using the province-level daily new confirmed case figures in Table 1 of that report, subtract the number reported for Nord-Kivu province for 26 November 2026 from the number reported for Ituri province for the same day. If that difference is 10 or more, the question resolves Yes; if it is 9 or less, the question resolves No. Only laboratory-confirmed cases count; suspected or probable cases do not.
question.fine_print: If the report's key-points summary and its Table 1 give different daily new confirmed case figures for a province for 26 November 2026, the Table 1 figures govern. If INSP publishes a corrected version (e.g. one marked "corrigé") of the SitRep for reporting date 26 November 2026, the corrected figures are used, provided that corrected version appears within 14 days of 27 November 2026. If that SitRep does not report province-level daily new confirmed case counts for 26 November 2026, the figures in the first subsequent INSP SitRep that does report them for that date are used. If no INSP publication ever reports province-level daily confirmed case counts for 26 November 2026, the question is annulled.

# Ituri vs Nord-Kivu daily new confirmed Ebola cases: research for 26 November 2026

**Bottom line:** Nothing settles this yet. Using the database's daily splits, Ituri reported at least 10 more new confirmed cases than Nord-Kivu on 19 of the 44 days from 2 October to 14 November (about 43%). That held on 6 of the last 14 days. Most of the daily figures I use come from a database whose method may not match Table 1 exactly, so treat these counts as approximate.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17: The ebola-tracker.org archive goes up to SitRep N°184 (reporting date 14 November). It does not yet have SitReps 185 or 186. It lists nine bulletins INSP never put online (N°003, 029, 043, 045, 063, 075, 076, 142, 172), so a missing SitRep is possible. [ebola-tracker](https://ebola-tracker.org/en/reports)
- 2026-11-14 (SitRep 184): 60 new confirmed cases nationally, 11,376 in total. Ituri had 28 new (7,858 total) and Nord-Kivu 25 new (2,860 total), a gap of +3. [database CSV](https://ebola-tracker.org/data/ebola-drc-database.csv)
- Caveat on the data: the database's daily "new_cases" is the site's own day-to-day change in cumulative totals, not necessarily the Table 1 figure. Its "lab_positives" column sometimes differs: Nord-Kivu shows 27 vs 17 on 21 October and 14 vs 24 on 6 November. I could not extract Table 1 from the PDF to check (the PDF text couldn't be read). [methodology](https://ebola-tracker.org/en/database)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. The reporting date is nine days away.
- Daily gap (Ituri minus Nord-Kivu), from the database:
  - 1-5 Nov: −20, −8 (rebuilt by the site because SitRep 172 was never published), −13, −6, −4
  - 6-10 Nov: +23, +12, +17, +13, +20
  - 11-14 Nov: −4, −1, +33 (40 vs 7), +3

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-16: The IOM sitrep counts 10,920 confirmed cases as of 7 November, still concentrated in Ituri and Nord-Kivu. [ReliefWeb](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/multi-country-bundibugyo-ebola-virus-disease-outbreak-situation-report-no-26-2-8-november-2026)
- 2026-11-16: 11,254 cases and 5,505 deaths as of 12 November. WHO says 400-500 new cases a week as the virus spreads into remote areas hit by violence. [Telangana Today](https://telanganatoday.com/dr-congo-ebola-outbreak-spreads-to-remote-areas-as-violence-hampers-response)
- 2026-11-15: AP reports the outbreak is still out of control six months in. [ITV](https://www.itv.com/news/2026-11-15/ebola-outbreak-remains-out-of-control-in-congo-after-6-months)
- 2026-11-12: WHO warns that insecurity is now a major obstacle to the response. A health centre treating Ebola patients was burned in Lolwa (Ituri). [actualite.cd](https://actualite.cd/2026/11/12/ebola-en-rdc-loms-alerte-sur-linsecurite-devenue-lun-des-plus-grands-obstacles-la)
- 2026-11-07: ACP reports 2,754 cumulative cases in Nord-Kivu as of 5 November. Beni (814) and Katwa (714) are the most affected zones. [ACP](https://acp.cd/province/trente-deux-nouveaux-cas-confirmes-enregistres-portant-le-cumul-a-2754-au-nord-kivu/)

## 4. Base rates (database daily splits)
- 2-27 October: the gap was 10 or more on 11 of 26 days. Those days were 3, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21 and 27 October; the 3 October figure was rebuilt by the site.
- 28 October-14 November: 8 of 18 days (28 and 31 October; 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13 November).
- Overall: 19 of 44 days, about 43%. Last 14 days: 6 of 14.
- Range of the gap: −26 (25 October, 32 vs 58) to +33 (13 November). Several days fell just short of 10: +8 on 20 October, +9 on 30 October.
- Ituri typically reports 20-47 new cases a day, Nord-Kivu 7-58. Both vary a lot from day to day.
- Weekly pattern (my tallies): Ituri ahead by 10 or more on 5 of 7 days in 6-12 October and 13-19 October, 1 of 7 in 20-26 October, 2 of 7 in 27 October-2 November, 4 of 7 in 3-9 November, and 2 of 5 in 10-14 November.
- Nord-Kivu's share has risen. WHO said Nord-Kivu supplied 640 of 1,463 cases in the 21 days to 3 November, with Ituri at 710.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on the daily split between the two provinces.
- The Kalshi and Polymarket Ebola markets (which countries will report a case, "pandemic in 2026" at about 1%) don't bear on this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Daily SitReps N°185-195 (15-25 November) will show whether the split is trending one way. N°196, with reporting date 26 November, is due on 27 November.
- Things that could move the numbers:
  - Attacks and disruption in Ituri (Lolwa, Mambasa and Mandima areas) can push Ituri's count down, or bunch up a backlog of results.
  - Lab backlogs in Beni, Katwa, Butembo or Mutwanga can spike Nord-Kivu's count.
  - Retrospective data reconciliation, as with the "harmonisation" notes on 30-31 October.
- A corrected ("corrigé") version of the 26 November SitRep would count if it appears by 11 December.

- In the most recent 13 bulletins (1-14 Nov), 6 days reached the threshold (46%). Over all 20 days, 9 did (45%). The median gap in the last 13 days is +3, and +9 over the 20.

- National daily totals are about 41-96, with a 7-day average of about 62-65.

- Things in reporting that could shift the split:
  - The Kasenyi strike in Ituri may continue, which can mean missing data.
  - Insecurity has kept the Butuhe checkpoint (Nord-Kivu) shut.
  - Provinces sometimes harmonise their data, as Ituri did on 30-31 Oct, though that changed totals rather than daily counts.
  - Nord-Kivu has received more Ervebo vaccine than other provinces (24,957 doses given nationally by 14 Nov). The vaccine wasn't developed for Bundibugyo virus, so its effect is uncertain.
- Release: SitRep N°196 (reporting date 26 Nov) is expected 27 Nov. Bulletins are sometimes never published, as with no. 172.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left and what Yes requires.** The outcome will be known in about 10 days, when SitRep N°196 (reporting date 26 Nov) is published on 27 Nov. Yes requires Ituri's daily new confirmed cases in Table 1 to exceed Nord-Kivu's by 10 or more for 26 November.

(b) **Status quo.** The most recent day (14 Nov) showed a gap of +3, which would resolve No. The typical median gap in recent weeks is about +3 to +9, just below the threshold. So the status quo leans slightly towards No.

(c) **Base rate.** Using daily splits from 2 Oct to 14 Nov, the gap was 10 or more on 19 of 44 days, about 43%. Over the last 20 bulletins it was 9 of 20 (45%), and over the last 13 it was 6 of 13 (46%). Reference value: about 43-45%.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - From 6 to 14 Nov Ituri led strongly: 315 vs 199 cases, an average gap of about 13 per day, with gaps of 10 or more on 6 of 9 days.
  - Ituri's lab positivity is high (25.6% on 13 Nov).
  - Ituri has many more affected health zones (28 vs 17).
- For No:
  - Nord-Kivu's share has been rising. In the 21 days to 3 Nov the split was 710 vs 640, an average gap of only about 3 per day.
  - Recent days were mixed: 11 Nov at −4, 12 Nov at −1, 14 Nov at +3.
  - The Beni cluster keeps producing spikes, such as 14 new cases in Beni on 14 Nov.
  - The Kasenyi treatment centre strike and insecurity in Ituri (Lolwa) can suppress Ituri's daily counts.
  - Nord-Kivu's count is erratic and can spike above Ituri's.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- No: Nord-Kivu reports about 25-30 cases (Beni, Katwa and Mutwanga keep producing), while Ituri reports about 30, or Kasenyi data are missing that day. The gap lands between −5 and +8.
- Yes: Ituri has a typical 35-45 day (Bunia and Mandima), and Nord-Kivu has a low day of 15-25. The gap reaches 10 or more, as it did on 6-10 Nov.

(f) **From base rate to final probability.** I start at about 44%. I adjust down slightly because:
- the medium-term trend shows Nord-Kivu's share rising,
- the most recent splits are near zero,
- the threshold sits a little above the median gap.

The roughly 13-per-day Ituri lead over 6-14 Nov partly offsets this. The daily noise is very large, with a standard deviation of about 15, so I stay close to the base rate. I move about 4 points down, to roughly 40%.

Probability: 40%

(a) The outcome will be known about 10 days from now, when SitRep N°196 (reporting date 26 November) appears on about 27 November. Yes requires Table 1's Ituri daily new confirmed count for 26 November minus Nord-Kivu's to be 10 or more.

(b) Status quo: the latest split (14 November) was Ituri 28 vs Nord-Kivu 25, a gap of +3, which would resolve No. The median gap over the last 13 days is about +3, so the typical day is a No.

(c) Base rate: across 44 days (2 October to 14 November), the gap reached 10 or more on 19 days, about 43%. In the last 13 to 20 bulletins it was about 45-46%. A reasonable reference rate is about 43%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Ituri led by 10 or more on 6 to 10 November (five days running) and again on 13 November (+33).
  - Ituri still has the larger caseload, typically 25-47 cases a day, and high lab positivity (25.6% on 13 November).
- For No:
  - Nord-Kivu's share of new cases has grown: 640 of 1,463 in the 21 days to 3 November (WHO, 6 November).
  - Beni is active, with 14 cases on 14 November, and there is a newer cluster in Mutwanga.
  - The Kasenyi treatment-centre strike in Ituri (noted 13 November) causes days with no data from that site, which lowers Ituri's count.
  - Insecurity in Ituri (the Lolwa attack, 12 November) may suppress case detection.
  - The 14 November gap was only +3.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: Nord-Kivu's Beni and Mutwanga clusters keep producing 25-35 cases a day, while Ituri reports in the high 20s or low 30s, held down by the Kasenyi strike and disruption. The gap ends up somewhere between −10 and +8.
- Yes: Ituri clears a lab backlog or Bunia surges to about 40 cases, while Nord-Kivu has a quiet day of about 15-20. The gap reaches +15 or more.

(f) I start from the 43% base rate. The daily gap is very noisy (−26 to +33), and with nine days to go, current trends add little information. I shade down slightly, by about 3 points, for three reasons:
- Nord-Kivu's rising share.
- Ituri reporting disruptions (the Kasenyi strike and insecurity).
- The structural asymmetry: Yes needs a gap of 10 or more, while the median gap is in single digits.

There are no relevant markets to anchor on.
